    // The 3-tuple built from the first three entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Number3, xs: Array<Number>): Number3
        => (xs[0], xs[1], xs[2]);

    // The 3-tuple with every component set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Number3, x: Number): Number3
        => (x, x, x);

    // The 4-tuple built from the first four entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Number4, xs: Array<Number>): Number4
        => (xs[0], xs[1], xs[2], xs[3]);

    // The 4-tuple with every component set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Number4, x: Number): Number4
        => (x, x, x, x);

    // The 8-lane tuple built from the first eight entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Number8, xs: Array<Number>): Number8
        => (xs[0], xs[1], xs[2], xs[3],
                   xs[4], xs[5], xs[6], xs[7]);

    // The 8-lane tuple with every lane set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Number8, x: Number): Number8
        => (x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x);

    // The 2D displacement built from the first two entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Vector2D, xs: Array<Number>): Vector2D
        => (xs[0], xs[1]);

    // The 2D displacement with both components set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Vector2D, x: Number): Vector2D
        => (x, x);

    // The 3D displacement built from the first three entries of xs.
    FromComponents(_: Vector3D, xs: Array<Number>): Vector3D
        => (xs[0], xs[1], xs[2]);

    // The 3D displacement with every component set to x.
    Broadcast(self: Vector3D, x: Number): Vector3D
        => (x, x, x);

    // The N-dimensional vector holding exactly the given components; the arity
    // is the length of xs.
    FromComponents(_: VectorN, xs: Array<Number>): VectorN
        => VectorN(xs);

    // The N-dimensional vector of the same arity as self with every component
    // set to x.
    Broadcast(self: VectorN, x: Number): VectorN
        => VectorN(self.Components.Count.Repeat(x));

    //==
    // # Derived functions for point-like types
    //
    // The per-concrete-type Euclidean distances that stand in for a generic metric
    // on the ICoordinate interface (`points.concepts.plato`), plus the barycentric
    // evaluation and normalization test for `points.types.plato`.

    //==
    // # ICoordinate
    //
    // A position in some space (IValue, IEquatable, IInterpolatable). ICoordinate is a
    // marker interface whose only operation is Lerp, and CoreAlgebra already ships
    // MidPoint, LerpClamped and SmoothLerp on IInterpolatable — which ICoordinate
    // inherits — so every interpolation convenience it can support already exists
    // upstream (SmoothLerp landed at algebra.library.plato) and no
    // ICoordinate-specific body is added here.
    //
    // TODO(interface-gap): a generic Distance over ICoordinate is out of reach, and
    // NOT via a cheap interface extension. All five implementors (Point2D, Point3D,
    // PointN in points.types.plato; UvCoordinate, UvwCoordinate in
    // points.types.plato) implement IOriginBased<TDelta> (hence
    // IDifference<TDelta>) — but each with a DIFFERENT delta type (Vector2D /
    // Vector3D / VectorN). So ICoordinate cannot inherit IDifference<TDelta>
    // without gaining a type parameter, which would cascade to
    // every bare `ICoordinate` mention tree-wide (a generic-arity change, not merely
    // an added obligation). `ICoordinate` therefore still does not inherit
    // IMetricSpace either: that would impose a concrete Distance on all five
    // implementors, including the two parametric ones. What DID change is that
    // the three Cartesian points now declare `IMetricSpace` individually
    // (points.types.plato) — they already had the body, so the declaration costs
    // nothing and makes the `IMetricSpace`-generic surface in
    // `algebra.library.plato` reachable.
    //
    // The Between-two-points delta is derivable for every IDifference implementor;
    // Distance is not, because it
    // additionally needs TDelta: INormed, and IDifference cannot bind that —
    // Instant's delta is a Duration, which is not INormed. A library function
    // cannot add the bound either (no `where` on library functions), so the six
    // Distance / DistanceSquared bodies below stay concrete.
    //
    // So the Euclidean distance is provided per concrete point type below, each as
    // `Between(a, b).Magnitude` over that type's own IDifference delta. This is the
    // sanctioned resolution: concrete functions rather than an interface obligation that
    // would force a generic-arity change on ICoordinate. DistanceSquared mirrors Distance without
    // the square root, for radius and nearest-neighbour comparisons.

    // The Euclidean distance between two 2D positions.
    Distance(a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Number
        => a.Between(b).Magnitude;

    // The squared Euclidean distance between two 2D positions; avoids the square root.
    DistanceSquared(a: Point2D, b: Point2D): Number
        => a.Between(b).MagnitudeSquared;

    // The Euclidean distance between two 3D positions.
    Distance(a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Number
        => a.Between(b).Magnitude;

    // The squared Euclidean distance between two 3D positions; avoids the square root.
    DistanceSquared(a: Point3D, b: Point3D): Number
        => a.Between(b).MagnitudeSquared;

    // The Euclidean distance between two N-dimensional positions.
    // Precondition: a and b have the same arity.
    Distance(a: PointN, b: PointN): Number
        => a.Between(b).Magnitude;

    // The squared Euclidean distance between two N-dimensional positions.
    // Precondition: a and b have the same arity.
    DistanceSquared(a: PointN, b: PointN): Number
        => a.Between(b).MagnitudeSquared;

    //==
    // # UvCoordinate / UvwCoordinate — the IOriginBased conversions
    //
    // Two lines each, and the whole affine surface (Add, Between, Subtract in
    // both spellings, Lerp, Origin) follows from them via
    // algebra.library.plato. These types previously declared
    // `implements IDifference<...>` without supplying bodies, so every derived
    // member was a throwing stub until Offset/FromOffset landed here.
    //
    // The origin is the parameter-space origin: (0, 0) is the UV origin defined
    // in CONVENTIONS.md (top-left, U right, V down), not a world-space point.

    // The parameter's displacement from the UV origin.
    Offset(uv: UvCoordinate): Vector2D
        => (uv.U, uv.V);

    // The parameter at the given displacement from the UV origin.
    FromOffset(_: UvCoordinate, v: Vector2D): UvCoordinate
        => (v.X, v.Y);

    // The parameter's displacement from the UVW origin.
    Offset(uvw: UvwCoordinate): Vector3D
        => (uvw.U, uvw.V, uvw.W);

    // The parameter at the given displacement from the UVW origin.
    FromOffset(_: UvwCoordinate, v: Vector3D): UvwCoordinate
        => (v.X, v.Y, v.Z);

## Reading this entry

Parameters before the colon are input values; the type after the parameter list is the result.
The first parameter also supplies the dot-call receiver. Type parameters on a declaration are
